test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: After allowing a discount of 50% on the marked price of an article, it is sold for ₹61,649. Find its marked price (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A 50% discount means the Selling Price is exactly 50% (or half) of the Marked Price.

Selling Price (SP) = 50% of Marked Price (MP)

⇒ MP = 2 × SP

⇒ MP = 2 × 61649 = 123298

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,23,298.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹61,649

Discount = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 
 MP = ? SP = ₹61,649 
 − 50% Discount 

**Calculations:**

Let the marked price be x.

⇒ Discount = 50% of x = 0.5x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = x − 0.5x = 0.5x

⇒ 0.5x = 61649

⇒ x = 61649 ÷ 0.5

⇒ x = 123298

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,23,298.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of the article. It is the reduction offered on the marked price.

Selling Price Formula

The selling price after a discount is calculated directly as: SP = MP × ((100 − Discount%) ÷ 100).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.
